## Goal

Collect producer answers in one batched interview for the prep items the provenance audit groups `needs-producer-input`, then clear each flag as its question is answered, so genuinely blocked prep items stop waiting on one-at-a-time producer attention.

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD (Scope item 4b). Discovered-from: WL-0MWTBJEI2008UGUR.

## Owner / queue

- **Owner:** producer (human interview batch).
- **Queue:** producer review — one batched session, answers recorded per item.

## Evidence rows that justify this item

Group counts: **1 can clear / 17 need producer input** (ContextHub 3, AI_Hell 4, SorraAgents 9, tce-the-rising 1). Two ContextHub rows (WL-0MWQYC2ZQ002NGZP, WL-0MWQYC3MZ0013YLS) were cleared externally at `22:00:04Z`/`22:00:05Z` after the `21:53Z` snapshot — re-read live before inviting them.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Re-read the live flagged set and group it with the provenance rule; record the exact list to be interviewed (expected seed: the 17 rows above, minus any already cleared).
2. Produce one batched interview document with, per item: the open question text, the deciding evidence comment id, the item's root and title, and a recommended option (advisory only).
3. Send the batch to the producer once; record the batch reference on WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD and on this item.
4. Record each producer answer in the item's Appendix (idempotent, never duplicate) and, on an answered row, clear `needsProducerReview` with an auditable comment.
5. Rows the producer does not answer stay flagged and grouped `needs-producer-input`; no silent clear and no dispatch of an unanswered row.
6. Record before/after flagged counts per root; no gate, budget or dispatcher-selection change.

Depends on the provenance audit's `needs-producer-input` grouping (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI).

No duplicate.

## Impact

Seventeen prep items that genuinely wait on the producer can be unblocked in one interview pass instead of one at a time, and each flag clears only when its question is answered. Outcome of the 2026-11-25 batch: **0 rows cleared against an answer, 16 still flagged, 1 newly flagged**; see reconciliation comment `WL-C0MWWF8FFZ0025U50` (one invited row, `AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3`, left the flagged set with no recorded answer and is reported as `cleared_without_answer`).

Dependency chain: snapshot → document → delivery → answer application → reconciliation. No duplicate children were created (idempotence: re-running reuses these ids).
- 2026-11-25T03:20Z — Reuse recorded: the provenance rule already exists as tested pure code (`classifyProducerReviewProvenance` / `assembleProducerReviewProvenance` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts`); no new rule is invented. WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P (packaged audit command) is referenced, not made a hard dependency, because the pure functions needed here already exist.
- 2026-11-25T03:20Z — AC coverage review run; all six parent acceptance criteria map to a child acceptance criterion.
- Effort/risk not re-estimated: the existing estimate (comment `WL-C0MWU4V95M0050NAI`: Small, Medium risk, 13.67h recommended) already covers this scope and decomposition does not change it.

data.description:
## Goal

As the operator, I can re-read the **live** producer-review-flagged prep set on every active root, grouped by the recorded provenance rule, so the batched interview invites exactly today's rows — not the 2026-11-23 snapshot — and every invited row shows why it is invited (question text, deciding evidence).

Parent: WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER — *Batch producer interviews for prep items grouped needs-producer-input*.

## Parent acceptance criterion covered

- Re-read the live flagged set and group it with the provenance rule; record the exact list to be interviewed (expected seed: the 17 rows above, minus any already cleared).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Re-read the live flagged set and group it with the provenance rule; record the exact list to be interviewed (expected seed: the 17 rows above, minus any already cleared).
- A read-only snapshot command returns, for every configured active root, each prep item carrying `needsProducerReview=true`, classified through the existing `classifyProducerReviewProvenance` + `assembleProducerReviewProvenance` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` — no second, hand-rolled provenance rule.
- For every row grouped `needs-producer-input` the snapshot emits: item id, root, title, the open question text, the deciding evidence comment id, and the flag age (`formatProducerReviewAge`), as both JSON and a markdown table.
- The command performs no write: it never calls `wl update`, `wl comment add`, `wl reviewed`, or any flag mutation — asserted by a test that fails if a write path is reached.
- Fixture tests cover at least three shapes: a `question-loop` row with an unanswered question; a `manual` row with no surviving evidence (fail-closed, e.g. `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23`, whose interview question is "does it still need producer attention?"); and a row cleared after the snapshot instant, which must be absent from live output.
- A live run is executed and its exact interview list — ids grouped by root, with the run timestamp — is recorded as a comment on WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER, noting any row in the 2026-11-23 seed that is now absent.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Test first: fixture-driven tests for the snapshot shape (three fixture rows above) plus the no-write assertion.
2. Thin read-only reader per root (`wl --worklog-dir <root>/.worklog list --json --needs-producer-review --include-not-started`, `comment list`, `audit-show`, `dep list`), reusing the existing collection shape documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Evidence commands (read-only)*.
3. Feed the collected evidence into the existing pure functions; map `ProducerReviewProvenanceTable` rows into an interview payload (id, root, title, question text, evidence comment id, flag age).
4. Emit JSON on stdout (machine path, for the next child) and a markdown summary on stderr/`--markdown`.
5. Record the live run's output as a comment on the parent item.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` (reuse: `classifyProducerReviewProvenance`, `assembleProducerReviewProvenance`, `formatProducerReviewAge`, `isProducerReviewQuestion`)
- `packages/herdr/src/producer-interview-snapshot.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/producer-interview-snapshot.test.ts` (new)
- `scripts/producer-interview-snapshot.ts` (new thin CLI wrapper)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (evidence commands + recorded audit the rule comes from)

## Constraints and out of scope

- Read-only: no flag is cleared and no item is reassigned by this child.
- Reuse, do not duplicate, WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P (packaged audit command, currently open). No hard dependency is recorded because the pure provenance functions this child needs already exist and are tested; if that item's command has landed when this is implemented, consume it instead of adding a second reader, and comment the substitution on both items.
- Cross-root coordination (ContextHub, AI_Hell, SorraAgents, tce-the-rising; games_curator and Tableau-Card-Engine were empty at the audit) must be configurable, not hard-coded to ContextHub.


## Impact

A batched producer interview can now be built from the live flagged set instead of last week's snapshot, so the producer is asked exactly the questions that are still open — and every invited row shows its item, root, question text, deciding evidence and flag age.
data.title: Interview snapshot and provenance grouping

data.description:
## Goal

As the producer, I receive **one** interview document listing every flagged prep row with its open question, so I can answer the whole batch in a single pass instead of being asked one item at a time.

Parent: WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER — *Batch producer interviews for prep items grouped needs-producer-input*.

## Parent acceptance criterion covered

- Produce one batched interview document with, per item: the open question text, the deciding evidence comment id, the item's root and title, and a recommended option (advisory only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Produce one batched interview document with, per item: the open question text, the deciding evidence comment id, the item's root and title, and a recommended option (advisory only).
- The document renders deterministically from the snapshot payload (`producer-interview-snapshot.ts --json`): identical input yields byte-identical output, and rows are grouped by root and numbered.
- Every row carries an explicit `**Recommended:** <option> — <one-line rationale>` line marked advisory only, per the shared interview contract §3 (SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ).
- A row with no surviving evidence renders the fail-closed question ("does it still need producer attention?") rather than being dropped or silently cleared.
- The document states, up front, how to answer (reply per row number), that unanswered rows stay flagged, and that answering is the authorisation for that row's flag clear.
- Tests assert that for every input row the rendered markdown contains its id, root, title, deciding evidence comment id, question text and exactly one `**Recommended:**` line; and that an empty input renders an explicit "no rows to interview" document rather than an empty file.
- The document is written to `docs/dev/producer-interview-batch-<UTC date>.md` and linked from a comment on WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Test first: snapshot fixture → expected markdown golden assertions (per-row field presence, one recommendation per row, empty-input case).
2. Pure renderer taking the snapshot payload and returning a markdown string — no I/O inside the renderer.
3. Write the markdown to `docs/dev/producer-interview-batch-<UTC date>.md`, with a stable header (batch id = snapshot timestamp, row count, per-root counts).
4. Recommend per row from the row's own evidence (dependency-held vs unanswered question vs no-evidence fail-closed); keep the recommendation advisory.
5. Comment the document path and row count on the parent item.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/producer-interview-batch-doc.ts` (new renderer)
- `packages/herdr/src/producer-interview-batch-doc.test.ts` (new)
- `scripts/producer-interview-batch-doc.ts` (new thin CLI wrapper)
- `docs/dev/producer-interview-batch-<UTC date>.md` (generated artefact)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (recorded audit table format to mirror)

## Constraints and out of scope

- Advisory recommendations only — the renderer never decides a row's fate.
- No delivery to the producer in this child (that is the next child); no flag mutation.

## Impact

The producer can answer every flagged prep item in one pass from a single numbered document, with each question and its advisory recommendation visible together instead of one item at a time.
data.title: Batch interview document renderer

data.description:
## Goal

As the producer, the batch reaches me exactly once, with a reference I can point at later, and both the originating remediation item and the batch item record it — so no row is asked twice and no row is silently assumed answered.

Parent: WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER — *Batch producer interviews for prep items grouped needs-producer-input*.

## Parent acceptance criterion covered

- Send the batch to the producer once; record the batch reference on WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD and on this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Send the batch to the producer once; record the batch reference on WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD and on this item.
- Exactly one delivery comment is posted on WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD and exactly one on WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER; each quotes the batch id (snapshot timestamp), the document path, the row count and per-root counts, and the list of invited item ids.
- Re-running delivery for the same batch id posts nothing and reports "already delivered" — proven by a test that runs delivery twice against a fake `wl` runner and counts posted comments.
- The delivery comment names how to answer (reply per row number in-session, or comment on the row's own item), states that unanswered rows stay flagged, and states that an answer is the authorisation for that row's clear.
- The delivery is recorded only after the document exists on disk and the snapshot is live — a stale document (older than the snapshot it claims) is refused with an error rather than delivered.
- WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD is `completed` / `in_review`: the reference comment is added without changing its status, stage or flags.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Test first: idempotent delivery (double run posts one comment), stale-document refusal, and the failure path when `wl` rejects the comment.
2. Delivery function taking batch id + document path + snapshot payload; composes the delivery comment text once and reuses it for both items.
3. Idempotency key: a stable marker in the comment (e.g. `[producer-interview-batch:<snapshot-timestamp>]`); a second run greps for the marker and exits 0 without posting.
4. Post to WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD first, then to WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER, recording both comment ids in the parent's completion comment.
5. **Producer gate:** after delivery, this chain genuinely waits on producer answers. The delivering session records the wait with `wl reviewed` where a hold is appropriate, and in either case **stops** rather than polling — the next child cannot proceed until answers exist.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/producer-interview-delivery.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/producer-interview-delivery.test.ts` (new)
- `scripts/producer-interview-deliver.ts` (new thin CLI wrapper)
- `docs/dev/producer-interview-batch-<UTC date>.md` (the artefact being delivered)

## Constraints and out of scope

- One batch, one delivery. No reminder loop, no per-row dispatch of questions.
- No flag clears in this child — clearing happens only against recorded answers (next child).

## Impact

The producer receives all 17 prep items that wait on them in a single answer sheet, delivered exactly once with a pinned batch reference on both the remediation item and the batch item — so no item is asked twice, none is silently assumed answered, and routine work stops queuing behind one-at-a-time producer attention.
data.title: Deliver batch once and record reference

data.description:
## Goal

As the operator, each producer answer is captured once, in the row's own worklog, and that row's producer hold is released with an auditable trail — so a cleared flag always points at the answer that justified it and no row is cleared by inference.

Parent: WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER — *Batch producer interviews for prep items grouped needs-producer-input*.

## Parent acceptance criterion covered

- Record each producer answer in the item's Appendix (idempotent, never duplicate) and, on an answered row, clear `needsProducerReview` with an auditable comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Record each producer answer in the item's Appendix (idempotent, never duplicate) and, on an answered row, clear `needsProducerReview` with an auditable comment.
- Each answer entry records: the question text as asked, the answer verbatim, the answering party, the batch id, and the evidence link (answer comment id) — appended to the row's own worklog (the Appendix), on the row's own root.
- Re-running for the same row and batch id updates the existing entry and does not add a duplicate, and does not post a second clear comment.
- On an answered row the hold is released with the documented mechanism for that root (`wl --worklog-dir <root>/.worklog reviewed <id> false` or equivalent `--needs-producer-review no`) plus a comment naming the answer comment id, the batch document path and the clearing agent. The clear is reversible and every clear names its justifying answer.
- A row with no recorded answer is never cleared: a test asserts that clearing a row without an answer raises and posts nothing.
- An answer of "keep waiting / do not proceed" is recorded as an answer and the row is **left flagged**, with the stated reason.
- Cross-root writes target only the originating root's store; nothing is re-created in ContextHub's worklog.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Test first: idempotent Appendix append, refusal to clear without an answer, and the "keep waiting" branch — all against a fake `wl` runner and a temporary worklog directory.
2. Answer-capture function: `(root, item id, batch id, question, answer, answering party)` → idempotent appendix comment; returns the comment id.
3. Clear function: takes the answer comment id, verifies the row is still flagged and the answer exists, then clears the flag and posts the audit comment ordering clear-after-answer.
4. CLI wrapper that accepts a batch answer file (row number → answer) so the producer's reply can be transcribed once and applied deterministically.
5. Record the applied clears as a comment on WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER (row id → answer comment id → clear comment id).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/producer-answer-capture.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/producer-answer-capture.test.ts` (new)
- `scripts/producer-interview-apply-answers.ts` (new thin CLI wrapper)
- `docs/dev/routine-vs-producer-handoff.md` (routine-vs-handoff rule the Appendix recording follows)
- `docs/dev/cross-repo-producer-review-restore.md` (cross-root clear mechanics)

## Constraints and out of scope

- **Producer gate:** this child cannot be completed without the producer's answers. On dispatch with no answers on record, the implement run records the outstanding question, hands off via `wl reviewed`, and stops — it must not clear anything by inference.
- No gate, budget or dispatcher-selection change.

## Impact

The producer can answer the whole batch once and each reply is durably recorded in that row's own worklog, so answered rows stop waiting while every cleared row can be traced back to the exact answer that justified it — and nothing is ever cleared without one.
data.title: Record answers and clear answered flags

data.description:
## Goal

As the operator, I can see — after the batch run — exactly what changed per root and can prove that the run touched nothing except the answered rows' flags: no gate, no budget and no dispatcher-selection behaviour moved.

Parent: WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER — *Batch producer interviews for prep items grouped needs-producer-input*.

## Parent acceptance criteria covered

- Rows the producer does not answer stay flagged and grouped `needs-producer-input`; no silent clear and no dispatch of an unanswered row.
- Record before/after flagged counts per root; no gate, budget or dispatcher-selection change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Rows the producer does not answer stay flagged and grouped `needs-producer-input`; no silent clear and no dispatch of an unanswered row.
- Record before/after flagged counts per root; no gate, budget or dispatcher-selection change.
- A reconciliation table is recorded on WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER with one row per root: flagged before, cleared against an answer, still flagged, and the total invited; the "before" side comes from the batch snapshot, the "after" side from a fresh re-run of the same snapshot command.
- Every cleared row in the table links to its answer entry and clear comment; a cleared row with no answer link fails the check rather than being reported as reconciled.
- Every unanswered row is asserted (in a test/check, not by eyeball) to still carry `needsProducerReview=true` and to still group `needs-producer-input` in the fresh re-run.
- The change set is asserted to contain no modification to dispatcher gating, audit budget or dispatcher-selection code paths (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-budget.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin*.ts`); the assertion command and its output are pasted into the completion comment.
- The item's `## Impact` line records how many rows were cleared and how many remain, with links to the reconciliation comment.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Test first: reconciliation renderer over two snapshot payloads (before/after) plus a fake answer map — covering a cleared row, an unanswered row, a "keep waiting" row, and the orphan-clear failure case.
2. Re-run the snapshot command from the first child at the end of the batch and diff the two grouped sets.
3. Render the per-root reconciliation table and post it on WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER.
4. Run the no-change assertion over the batch's diff range and record its output with the table.
5. Update `## Impact` with the cleared/remaining counts.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/producer-interview-reconcile.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/producer-interview-reconcile.test.ts` (new)
- `scripts/producer-interview-reconcile.ts` (new thin CLI wrapper)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (must be unchanged — asserted, not edited)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (where the reconciliation record is referenced from)

## Constraints and out of scope

- Verification and reporting only: no flag mutation, no gating change.
- Runs last, after answers are applied; it may legitimately report "0 cleared, N still flagged" when the producer has not answered.

## Impact

After the batch the operator can see, per root, that **0 rows were cleared against an answer** and **16 remain flagged** `needs-producer-input` (17 invited), with the one silent clear (`AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3`) called out as a failure rather than reconciled — see the [reconciliation record](comment:WL-C0MWWF8FFZ0025U50) on WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER.
data.title: Reconciliation and no-change verification
